about: Entirely fictional acceptance cases (status family K-3 with sub-codes K-3-1 seagrass-mat weaver, K-3-2 brassware smith, K-3-3 knot-craft maker, K-3-4 folding-fan trainee; the other-family codes L-6 and L-6-1; invented agency 가상 누리별이주청 (the 'Nuribyeol agency'), regions 가상 별무리 관할 / 가상 갈대숲 관할, office 가상 이음 출장소, documents 가상 K-3 체류 길잡이, 가상 K-3 국외 체류자 안내문, K-3 Craft Residence Handbook (fictional), Cẩm nang lưu trú K-3 (giả định), K-3 Abroad Residents Handbook (fictional), 가상 K-3 수수료·처리기간 안내, amounts and dates); not law. Authored only from trusted_evidence_spec.md (005-X revision: 고르는 질문의 코드별 부분, a choice question not split otherwise is asked one choice code at a time with choice_part, contract v18, and the answers are joined in question order; 고르는 질문 부분의 값 검사, the value_retry and withholding of a value still swapped; with the 005-W choice_codes, the 005-V choice_retry, the 005-U conflict_records, the 005-T status retry, the 005-S cap and 005-R two-case paragraphs, the sub-code and situation splits and section 6); the 005-W acceptance suite was read for format only (schema, case keys, registry shape, the expected block, how split cases list model_statuses, mention-group and forbidden-pattern notation), the gate v19 constants, validate_suite and registry_for for structure, the 005-W manifest thresholds, and evidence_registry for content_sha256 and record_problems. No implementation, run output, test, review file or other suite's expected results were read, the pipeline was not run, and all questions, records and patterns were written fresh; other suites were searched only for duplicate questions and reused names. Focus, choice questions (spec 4 and 5, 005-X): two sibling sub-codes with a choosing word and one admissible record naming both, so the question gets choice_codes and is split into one part per choice code; model_statuses lists one status per part. Choice cases, one per category: A05X-02 (vi, right code second, own-sentence values), A05X-22 (en, right code second, own-sentence values, historical date with a not-yet-effective successor), A05X-33 (vi, right code first, own-sentence values, also a not-conflict), A05X-45 (ko question, English evidence, right code first, own-sentence values), A05X-62 (en, right code second, own-sentence values), A05X-70 (ko, one shared sentence naming both codes with one value, so the value check does not apply and both codes match). Choice questions ask a comparison (shorter, lower, longer, less) rather than quoting a value, except A05X-70, so that a correct part for the non-matching code has no reason to restate a number the value check would read as the other code's. Choice near-misses: A05X-18 (a sub-code with its own parent K-3), A05X-58 (second code L-6 never named by the evidence), A05X-60 (two codes without a choosing word), A05X-81 (a choosing question whose records are each limited to one sub-code, so the 005-J sub-code split applies and each part gets only its own record and no choice_codes). Kept from 005-W: conflict-template cases A05X-28, 29, 30, 44, 56, 59, 67 (28, 29, 30, 44, 67 ask what each text says); not-conflicts A05X-31, 32, 33; partial traps A05X-36, 42, 61; cap positives A05X-01, 03, 37; two-case positives A05X-16, 40, 43; role reversal A05X-14, 25, 78. Ambiguities recorded: (1) Spec 4 (005-X) says each part writes what the evidence says about its choice_part and whether that code is the one sought; the joined first answer therefore carries both codes and, where the evidence gives per-code values, both values, which are the mention groups. (2) Spec 5 (005-X) checks numbers in part sentences that do not name another choice code; a number taken from the question (for example a quoted fee in 'which code pays 45,000 won?') would count as the other code's value in the non-matching part, so value-quoting choice questions were avoided where a per-code value exists. (3) Whether the 'two in Korean, two in English, two in Vietnamese' split refers to the question or the reply language does not matter here: every choice case has the same question and reply language except A05X-45, whose question and reply are both Korean (only its evidence is English). (4) Spec 5 (005-J) joins sub-code parts 'in sub-code order'; in A05X-79, 80 and 81 the evidence order, the question order and the sorted order agree. (5) 'or', 'hay' and 'nào' also occur inside other words (for, report, thay); every question with two sibling codes either has a whole-word choosing word or is Korean with none, and no two-code question contains 'thay'. (6) No forbidden pattern binds a value to a code; value patterns forbid inadmissible values only, and choice patterns fire only on a stated conclusion naming the wrong code; each was tested with correct value-first answers in its language. (7) Mention groups assume the 005-S normalisation (lower case, whitespace removed).

Each English sentence puts the value before its code; the sentence (not the word order) is what the 005-X value check uses. One admissible record names both codes (status_scope has both), so there is no sub-code split (spec 4, 005-J: every record must have exactly one sub-code) and no location split, and with one record there is no conflict pair (005-U). Each part names its code, cites the record and says whether that code is the one sought, without the other code's value; the parts are joined in question order, so the raw channel's first answer contains both codes and both fees. Each code has its own sentence with its own value (K-3-2: 24,000 won; K-3-4: 57,000 won), so the 005-X value check applies: a part that writes the other code's value in a sentence not naming the other code is asked once more (value_retry) and withheld if it still does.
